episode.title: Isolate stdio child-process diagnostics from the interactive terminal
episode.before: At parent commit 7db2703b332bbe8afe2c89b1fed2dd8c03cbd9af, the stdio server lifecycle invoked stdio_client(server_params) without an errlog argument. The SDK therefore used its stderr default, allowing child startup banners and logs to write to the parent process's interactive terminal while the terminal UI was rendering.
episode.after: At commit 379b2273d95566e8a69eadabceabc6ee08521b49, the process lazily opens and reuses a thread-safe, append-mode, line-buffered diagnostic file with a real file descriptor; falls back first to the null device and finally to parent stderr; writes a best-effort timestamped server-start marker; and supplies the resulting handle as errlog whenever a stdio server is spawned. Normal session initialization, PID tracking, reconnection, and shutdown remain on the existing lifecycle path.
episode.diff: The implementation modifies only tools/mcp_tool.py: it adds sys and datetime imports, a locked process-wide stderr-handle cache, diagnostic-sink creation and fallback logic, a timestamped header writer, and changes the single stdio_client call from stdio_client(server_params) to stdio_client(server_params, errlog=_errlog) after obtaining the shared sink. The commit reports 81 insertions and 1 deletion; no test file changed.

evidence_units.claim: The parent implementation called stdio_client(server_params) without supplying errlog at the stdio subprocess-spawn boundary.
The resolution commit identifies unsolicited child stderr writes to the user's terminal during concurrent prompt_toolkit/Rich rendering as the cause of display corruption and reported hangs.

The new sink provider uses a lock and process-wide cache, creates the profile logs directory, opens mcp-stderr.log in append mode with line buffering and replacement decoding, verifies fileno(), and reuses the handle.

If the diagnostic log cannot be opened, sink acquisition attempts the null device and uses parent stderr only as a final fallback so server startup is not rejected solely because logging setup failed.
Before spawning a server, the implementation best-effort writes and flushes a timestamped marker containing the server name into the shared diagnostic stream; marker-write failures are ignored.
The stdio lifecycle writes the start marker, acquires the sink, and passes it as the errlog argument to stdio_client while retaining the existing PID tracking and client-session initialization flow.
The pinned change modifies only tools/mcp_tool.py, with 81 insertions and 1 deletion; the behavioral call-site change adds the explicit errlog argument.
evidence_units.source: git diff --stat and git diff 7db2703b332bbe8afe2c89b1fed2dd8c03cbd9af 379b2273d95566e8a69eadabceabc6ee08521b49 -- tools/mcp_tool.py

evidence_units.claim: An existing mocked lifecycle test starts a stdio server, verifies session initialization and tool discovery, and shuts it down, but it does not assert the errlog argument or diagnostic-file behavior.
The commit records an end-to-end check that spawned a subprocess with the log file descriptor as stderr and observed banner lines in the log with no output reaching the calling terminal.
No test file was added or modified by the pinned implementation commit.

candidate_atomics.name: provision-reusable-child-diagnostic-sink
candidate_atomics.title: Provision a reusable file-descriptor-backed diagnostic sink
candidate_atomics.description: Create one process-wide sink suitable for direct child-process stderr attachment, while preserving startup through bounded fallback behavior when the preferred log cannot be opened.

semantic_action.intent: Provide child processes with a non-interactive diagnostic destination without making optional logging setup a hard startup dependency.
semantic_action.pre_state: A child process is about to be spawned, but no reusable, file-descriptor-backed diagnostic sink has been acquired for its stderr.
semantic_action.post_state: A cached writable handle is available: preferably an append-mode profile log, otherwise the null device, with parent stderr retained only as the final degraded fallback.
semantic_action.validation: Verify that repeated acquisition returns the cached handle, the preferred handle exposes fileno(), and forced log-open failure selects the documented fallback path.

candidate_atomics.name: annotate-shared-child-diagnostic-stream
candidate_atomics.title: Mark each child launch in the shared diagnostic stream
candidate_atomics.description: Write a best-effort timestamped producer marker before launch so output from multiple children remains attributable without introducing a pipe or reader thread.

semantic_action.intent: Keep diagnostics from multiple child processes distinguishable in a shared append-only destination.
semantic_action.pre_state: A shared diagnostic sink has been selected and a named child process is about to start.
semantic_action.post_state: When the sink accepts writes, it contains a flushed timestamped start marker identifying the child; marker failure does not block launch.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the sink for a flushed marker containing the supplied child name and confirm that a marker-write exception does not escape the annotation operation.

candidate_atomics.name: route-child-stderr-away-from-interactive-terminal
candidate_atomics.title: Bind child stderr to the selected diagnostic sink
candidate_atomics.description: Pass the selected handle explicitly at the subprocess client boundary so child diagnostics do not use the library's implicit parent-stderr destination.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent unsolicited child diagnostics from corrupting or blocking an independently rendered interactive terminal while retaining file-based diagnostics when possible.
semantic_action.pre_state: The stdio client is invoked without an explicit stderr destination, so child diagnostics may inherit the parent process's interactive stderr.
semantic_action.post_state: The stdio client receives an explicit errlog handle, while its existing session initialization, PID tracking, reconnect, and shutdown behavior remains in place.
semantic_action.validation: Spawn a child that writes a known banner to stderr and prove that the banner reaches the selected sink but not the calling terminal; also exercise the existing start-and-shutdown lifecycle.

candidate_workflows.name: isolate-subprocess-diagnostics-from-terminal-ui
candidate_workflows.title: Isolate subprocess diagnostics from an interactive terminal UI
candidate_workflows.description: Establish a reusable file-descriptor-backed diagnostic destination, optionally identify each producer in a shared stream, and explicitly bind child stderr at the spawn boundary without changing the subprocess protocol or lifecycle.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure diagnostics emitted by stdio-managed child processes do not write into and destabilize the parent application's interactive terminal, while keeping those diagnostics inspectable when the preferred log is available.
when_to_use: A library-managed child process defaults stderr to the parent process's terminal.
The parent concurrently renders an interactive terminal interface whose state can be corrupted by unsolicited writes.
Child stderr is diagnostic output rather than the protocol stream used for parent-child communication.
anti_goals: Do not redirect or modify the child's protocol-bearing stdin or stdout streams.
Do not redesign PID tracking, session initialization, reconnection, cancellation, or shutdown behavior.
Do not add a per-line pipe and reader thread solely to prefix diagnostics when a launch marker is sufficient.
Do not make failure to open an optional diagnostic log prevent the child from starting.
not_applicable_when: Child stderr is itself a required machine-readable protocol channel.
The parent intentionally exposes child stderr directly to a non-interactive caller.
The subprocess API cannot accept a file descriptor or equivalent explicit stderr destination.
Policy requires startup to fail rather than discard diagnostics when durable logging is unavailable.
inputs: subprocess spawn call site and stderr-option contract
workflow_graph.entry_state: A stdio child is launched through a library call that omits the stderr destination, allowing diagnostic output to inherit the interactive parent stderr.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Every affected stdio spawn explicitly receives the selected diagnostic handle; preferred-path child stderr is written to the shared log rather than the terminal; producer launches are best-effort labeled; and the pre-existing connection lifecycle remains operational.

steps.condition: Before the first affected child is spawned, and thereafter through the cached handle.
steps.validation: Confirm a real file descriptor is returned for the preferred append-mode log, repeated calls reuse it, and log-open failure follows the bounded fallback chain.

steps.condition: Use when multiple named children can write to the same sink and launch attribution is useful; annotation must remain best effort.
steps.validation: Confirm the marker includes the child identity and timestamp, is flushed before spawn, and cannot abort startup if its write fails.

steps.condition: At every subprocess-spawn call site whose implicit stderr destination is the interactive parent stream.
steps.validation: Capture both destinations while a child emits a known stderr banner; require the preferred sink to contain the banner and the terminal capture not to contain it, then confirm initialization and shutdown still complete.

validation_ladder: Static boundary check: verify each affected spawn supplies an explicit stderr/errlog destination instead of relying on the library default.
Sink contract check: verify the preferred destination is append-mode, promptly flushed or line-buffered, reusable, and exposes the OS-level descriptor required by subprocess machinery.
Fallback check: force preferred-log creation failure and confirm startup can proceed through the null-device path; document the final parent-stderr degradation if even that open fails.
Lifecycle regression check: start the mocked stdio connection, initialize and discover tools, then shut it down successfully.
End-to-end isolation check: spawn a real child that writes a recognizable stderr payload and assert it appears in the diagnostic log but not in the terminal capture.
stop_conditions: Stop and redesign if stderr carries required protocol messages rather than diagnostics.
Stop if the subprocess library cannot attach the chosen sink directly or the sink lacks the required OS-level descriptor.
Do not claim complete terminal isolation when sink acquisition reaches the final parent-stderr fallback.
Do not claim automated regression coverage until a test directly asserts routing and terminal non-leakage.
unresolved_or_deferred: The pinned commit contains no automated test directly asserting the new errlog argument, preferred log contents, fallback selection, or absence of terminal output.
The reported end-to-end verification is described in the commit message, but its command, fixture, and captured output are not present in the checkout or evidence bundle.
The process-wide diagnostic handle is not explicitly closed by this change; its intended lifetime is described as once per process, but shutdown cleanup is not separately tested.
If both the preferred log and null device cannot be opened, the implementation intentionally degrades to parent stderr and therefore cannot guarantee terminal isolation.

unresolved_questions: GitHub issue body, comments, review discussion, and status checks are unavailable in the supplied evidence bundle.
Was the reported end-to-end verification executed in CI or only manually? The available evidence does not establish this.
Should a future regression test reset and close the process-wide handle between cases to verify preferred, null-device, and final-degradation paths independently?
